classification.difficultyReason: Combine rectangle and square diagonal properties with triangle, straight-line and parallel-line angle reasoning.

content.prompt: Use the properties of rectangles and squares to find the values of $x$, $y$, $z$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ in the diagrams below, giving reasons.

spec.description: Landscape rectangle with four right-angle marks and red dashed diagonals meeting at M; each half-diagonal retains its source label.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a rectangle; AM=10 cm, MC=x, MB=y, DM=z.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and unknowns are visible.

answer.worked: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so $AM=MC=MB=MD$. Since $AM=10\text{ cm}$, $x=y=z=10\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: PQRS retains opposite-side parallel marks, matching double length ticks on PQ and PS, the right angle at S, and red dashed diagonals.
spec.mathematics: O is the diagonal intersection; alpha is angle QOR and beta is angle PQO.

answer.worked: The opposite sides are parallel, so $PQRS$ is a parallelogram. Its right angle makes it a rectangle, and its equal adjacent sides make it a square. A square's diagonals meet at right angles, so $\alpha=90^\circ$. Its diagonals bisect the vertex angles, so $\beta=90^\circ\div2=45^\circ$.

spec.description: Portrait rectangle with opposite-side parallel marks, a right angle at I, red dashed diagonals, and an external curved leader to the given angle at H.
spec.mathematics: Angle GHF=30 degrees; theta=angle GFH, alpha=angle FTG, beta=angle FTI, gamma=angle FIT.
spec.answerVisibility: The given 30-degree angle is visible; all four requested angles remain unknown.

answer.short:
$\alpha=60^\circ$, $\beta=120^\circ$, $\gamma=30^\circ$, $\theta=60^\circ$.

Use equal half-diagonals to form isosceles triangle $FTI$.
answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $FGH$,
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-30^\circ\\\theta&=60^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
Since $FI\parallel GH$, alternate angles give $\angle IFT=30^\circ$. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so $FT=IT$. Thus triangle $FTI$ is isosceles and $\gamma=30^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\beta&=180^\circ-30^\circ-30^\circ\\\beta&=120^\circ\\\alpha&=180^\circ-120^\circ\\\alpha&=60^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The last step uses a straight angle at $T$.

spec.description: Subdivided rectangle retains DE, EF, all parallel marks, the right angle at A, matching length ticks on BC and FC, and the full beta arc spanning ED to EB across EF.
spec.mathematics: E lies on AB; F lies on DC; angle EDF=40 degrees; alpha=angle AED; beta=angle DEB, not angle FEB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 40-degree angle is visible.

answer.worked:
Since $AE\parallel DF$, alternate angles give $\alpha=\angle EDF=40^\circ$. Angles $AED$ and $DEB$ form a straight angle at $E$:
$$\begin{aligned}\beta&=180^\circ-40^\circ\\\beta&=140^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
